nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms η-carbide-type structure of Co_{3-x}Fe_xMo_3N with diffraction peaks at 40.06°, 42.6°, and 46.58° corresponding to (422), (511), and (440) planes; peaks shift negatively with increasing Fe content while structure is preserved.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 1a, the successful substitution of Co by Fe was confirmed by X-ray diffraction (XRD). The diffraction peaks around 40.06°, 42.6°, and 46.58° are corresponding to the (422), (511), and (440) lattice planes of Co₃Mo₃N, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM of Co_{2.5}Fe_{0.5}Mo_3N shows interplanar spacings of 0.637, 0.391 and 0.214 nm indexed to (220) plane.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscopy (TEM) analysis of Co_{2.5}Fe_{0.5}Mo_3N is consistent with the XRD patterns (Figure 1d, e), which show that the interplanar spacings of 0.637, 0.391 and 0.214 nm can be indexed to the plane (220) of Co_{2.5}Fe_{0.5}Mo_3N.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows Co_{2.5}Fe_{0.5}Mo_3N and Co₃Mo₃N consist of clavate particles with approximate size of 200 nm and similar morphologies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images of Co_{2.5}Fe_{0.5}Mo_3N and Co₃Mo₃N (Figures S3 and S4) display that they consist of clavate particles with approximate size of 200 nm and have similar morphologies.

nodes.characterization_summary: BET surface area of Co_{2.5}Fe_{0.5}Mo_3N is 4 m²/g, slightly bigger than Co₃Mo₃N at 3.3 m²/g.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The results of N₂ adsorption-desorption analysis are presented in Figures S5 and S6, where the BET surface area of Co_{2.5}Fe_{0.5}Mo_3N (4 m²g⁻¹) is slightly bigger than that of Co₃Mo₃N (3.3 m²g⁻¹).

nodes.characterization_summary: Four-point probe measurement shows electronic conductivity of Co_{2.5}Fe_{0.5}Mo_3N at 200 S cm^{-1} at 10 MPa, 4-5 orders of magnitude higher than corresponding oxides.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electronic conductivity of Co_{2.5}Fe_{0.5}Mo_3N at 10 MPa is around 200 S cm^{-1}. Such an impressive conductivity is superior to that of the previously reported transition metal nitrides.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS measurements (Table S1) indicate negligible difference between actual and controlled mole ratios of Co:Fe:Mo for synthesized Co_{3-x}Fe_xMo_3N.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Table S1 of the Supporting Information presents the data of inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) measurements of the synthesized Co_{3-x}Fe_xMo_3N, indicating that there is negligible difference between the actual and controlled mole ratios of Co:Fe:Mo.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER Co_{2.5}Fe_{0.5}Mo_3N shows core-shell structure with crystalline core (lattice spacing 0.636 nm for (111) plane) and amorphous oxide shell.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 4a and Figure S15a, a core-shell structure is formed and the surficial Co_{2.5}Fe_{0.5}Mo_3N transforms into an amorphous layer... the lattice fingers with a spacing of 0.636 nm can be assigned to the (111) plane of Co_{2.5}Fe_{0.5}Mo_3N.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER Co_{2.5}Fe_{0.5}Mo_3N shows Co 2p peaks at 780.0, 795.0 eV (Co³⁺ in CoOOH) and 781.5, 796.7 eV (Co²⁺ in Co(OH)₂); Co³⁺/Co²⁺ ratio = 1.29; O 1s peaks at 530.2 eV (OH⁻), 531.4 eV (M-O), 532.4 eV (adsorbed H₂O).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co 2p spectrum of Co_{2.5}Fe_{0.5}Mo_3N is shown in Figure 4c. The fitted peaks located at 780.0, 795.0 eV and 781.5, 796.7 eV are attributed to Co³⁺ in CoOOH and Co²⁺ in Co(OH)₂, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping and line-scan of pristine Co_{2.5}Fe_{0.5}Mo_3N prove surface oxidation after air exposure, leading to coexistence of oxygen and nitrogen and oxynitride phase formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Meanwhile, as illustrated in Figure S2, the energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) mapping and line-scan results prove that the oxidation of the pristine Co_{2.5}Fe_{0.5}Mo_3N occurs after exposure to the air.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER Co_3Mo_3N shows increased Co^{3+} species and disappearance of Co^0 peaks compared to pre-OER sample, confirming surface reconstruction to oxygen-rich layer during OER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Taking Co_3Mo_3N as an example, the peaks of Co^0 species disappear and the peaks of Co^{3+} species arise after the OER (Figure S18a), which confirms that Co_3Mo_3N undergoes a surface reconstruction process during the OER.

nodes.characterization_summary: Nyquist plots (Figure S9) show significantly lower charge-transfer resistance (R_ct) for Co_{2.5}Fe_{0.5}Mo_3N compared to Co_3Mo_3N.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Nyquist plots in Figure S9 reveal that the charge-transfer resistance (R_ct) of Co_{2.5}Fe_{0.5}Mo_3N is significantly lower than that of Co_3Mo_3N.
